children: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he does not expect to become President Donald Trump’s new AI czar, pushing back on reports that had identified him as a leading candidate for the newly proposed role.

Asked on Fox News whether Trump had asked him to take the position, Bessent said, “I would think that is probably fake news,” while adding that he would “continue being a part of the administration AI effort.” When asked whether he would want the job, Bessent said, “I think there is one AI czar, and that's President Trump.”

Bessent's comments came after media reports stated that he has emerged as a frontrunner for the position, citing three people familiar with the matter. The White House had said that reports about personnel decisions that had not been officially announced should be regarded as speculation.

that he would create an “AI Force” and appoint an AI “czar,” without providing details on how either initiative would be structured. He compared the proposed force with the Space Force, which he established during his first term.

Bessent has remained involved in the administration's AI discussions. He recently held talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng that included a proposed mechanism for communicating about AI incidents that could pose national-security risks, as well as a potential U.S.-China dialogue on AI.

The Treasury secretary had also been among the names discussed for the new position after prediction-market traders had identified him as a leading candidate. Trump has not publicly named an AI czar, and the administration's final choice remained unsettled.

title: Bessent pulls the plug on AI czar rumors
